summary: The main article describes a mesoionic carbene (MIC) catalyzed coupling of aldehydes and alkyl halides, demonstrating how the choice of base (weak vs. strong) controls the reaction pathway (ionic vs. radical). The document includes optimization tables, substrate scope tables, and mechanistic studies including radical clock experiments and DFT calculations.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: NHC- and MIC-catalyzed ionic and radical coupling reactions.
items.description: This figure illustrates the two distinct pathways (ionic and radical) in NHC/MIC organocatalysis and highlights the limitation of classical NHCs in controlling these pathways compared to MICs.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions a
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of catalysts, solvents, bases, and temperatures to optimize the yield of ketone 3aa and alpha-alkylated benzoin 4aa.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of the coupling reaction of aldehydes and alkyl halides
items.description: This table displays the substrate scope for various aryl aldehydes and alkyl halides under the optimized ionic coupling conditions.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Reaction of aldehydes with complex secondary alkyl iodides.
items.description: This figure shows the stereochemical outcomes of reactions involving complex secondary alkyl iodides to probe the SN2 nature of the ionic pathway.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Scope of the coupling reaction of aldehydes and alkyl halides
items.description: This table details the synthesis of alpha-alkylated benzoin derivatives and cyclic ethers when the reaction is performed in methanol.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Mechanism study.
items.description: This figure presents radical clock experiments, inhibition studies, and a proposed catalytic cycle involving a tandem benzoin condensation/retro-benzoin sequence.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Comparison of MIC catalyzed coupling reactions with Cs2CO3 and t BuOK.
items.description: A comparative summary showing how different bases lead to distinct chemical behaviors and product distributions based on the intermediate (BI vs BI-).

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: NHC-catalyzed coupling reaction of aldehydes and the calculated p K a of BIs.
items.description: This figure shows the calculated pKa values for various NHC-derived Breslow intermediates to explain the base-controlled selectivity.
